obligations.summary: Providers must establish, implement, document, and maintain a risk management system in relation to high-risk AI systems.

The risk management system must operate as a continuous iterative process throughout the entire lifecycle of the high-risk AI system, comprising identification and analysis of known and reasonably foreseeable risks, estimation and evaluation of risks under intended use and foreseeable misuse, evaluation of risks from post-market monitoring data, and adoption of targeted risk management measures.

Risk management measures must give due consideration to the combined effects and interactions of all applicable requirements in order to minimise risks while achieving an appropriate balance in fulfilling those requirements.

Risk management measures must ensure that residual risks associated with each hazard and the overall residual risk of the high-risk AI system are judged to be acceptable, through elimination or reduction of risks via design and development, implementation of mitigation and control measures for risks that cannot be eliminated, and provision of information and training to deployers as required.
exceptions: Elimination or reduction of risks is required only insofar as technically feasible.

obligations.summary: High-risk AI systems must be tested to identify appropriate risk management measures, ensure consistent performance for the intended purpose, and verify compliance with the requirements of this Section.

Testing of high-risk AI systems must be performed at appropriate points throughout the development process and, in any event, prior to placement on the market or putting into service, against pre-defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds appropriate to the intended purpose.
exceptions: Testing procedures may include real-world condition testing in accordance with Article 60.

obligations.summary: When implementing the risk management system, providers must consider whether the high-risk AI system is likely to have an adverse impact on persons under the age of 18 and, as appropriate, other vulnerable groups.

For providers of high-risk AI systems already subject to internal risk management requirements under other Union law, the risk management aspects under Article 9 may be integrated into or combined with those existing risk management procedures.
exceptions: Providers subject to existing Union law risk management requirements may combine or integrate Article 9 obligations with those existing procedures rather than maintaining entirely separate processes.
